record.title: OpenAI reports a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model developed with GPT-6 Astra
record.summary: A Nov 15 OpenAI science post describes a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model, linking an Oct 6 preprint by Nathaniel Craig. The paper proposes a gauge-invariant fermion measure for overlap fermions on finite four-dimensional lattices under an admissibility bound. Its author reports a Lean formalization whose proof terms compiled and passed separate kernel replay and axiom checks. OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra materially contributed to the refinement strategy and detailed proof, with outside lattice theorists reviewing drafts. This remains an author-reported mathematical construction: finite-spacing reflection positivity, efficient evaluation of the complete current, and an interacting continuum limit are open; practical lattice simulations are not yet established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published a science post on 15 November 2026 describing a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model and linking Nathaniel Craig’s arXiv:2610.09093 preprint, which was submitted on 6 October 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports a nonperturbative gauge-invariant measure for overlap fermions on finite four-dimensional lattices in a class of nonabelian chiral gauge theories including the Standard Model, under a sufficiently small plaquette admissibility bound. The author presents this as a candidate lattice definition; it is not a demonstrated practical simulation framework.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author’s Lean verification report says all 16 modules compiled with no errors or warnings, 95,810 exported declarations passed a separate Lean kernel replay, and the axiom check accepted only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound with no sorryAx. The same report records that its configured comparator-reference command failed on generated proof-name differences; the proof checks described above were run separately and passed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI and the paper’s author say GPT-6 Astra was essential to the refinement strategy and detailed proof, while human lattice field theorists reviewed drafts and asked probing questions. This is a first-party account, not an independent attribution study.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The sources do not establish finite-spacing reflection positivity, efficient evaluation of the complete current, a fully interacting continuum limit, or readiness for realistic lattice simulations; the paper and its mathematical companion explicitly leave these questions open.

evidence_gaps.description: This activation did not independently replay the delivered Lean project/archive or obtain specialist independent review of its mathematical construction and assumptions.

Finite-spacing reflection positivity, an efficient implementation of the complete current, and an interacting continuum limit are explicitly unresolved; the source says the construction is not yet a practical simulation answer.

brief.importance_rationale: If the candidate nonperturbative lattice construction is mathematically sound and its open physical conditions are resolved, it would address a foundational problem affecting theoretical physics. This is potentially field-shaping consequence; it does not imply that the present evidence is independently confirmed or practically usable.
limitations: The construction and Lean verification outcomes are reported by the paper author; the research desk did not independently reproduce or replay them.

The paper is bounded to finite periodic lattices and an admissibility condition on gauge fields; it is a candidate mathematical definition, not evidence of useful numerical simulation or phenomenological output.
The author report records a failed comparator-reference check due to generated proof-name differences even though separate compilation, axiom and kernel checks passed.
Finite-spacing reflection positivity, efficient evaluation of the complete current and an interacting continuum limit remain open.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports a gauge-invariant measure for overlap fermions and a candidate nonperturbative definition for the Standard Model on finite periodic four-dimensional lattices under an admissibility bound. It also reports formal Lean proofs for the mathematical companion.
technical.demonstrated_result: This activation inspected the linked preprint, mathematical companion and Lean verification report. Their mathematical and proof-check outcomes remain author-reported; the research desk did not replay the project.
technical.mechanism: The construction reconstructs a smooth connection from coarse gauge links, samples it on progressively finer lattices, and uses comparisons of neighboring overlap-fermion chiral projectors to build a measure current. Summing the refinement contributions is reported to cancel intermediate return phases and satisfy local/global integrability under the stated assumptions.
technical.regime: Finite periodic four-dimensional lattices with sufficiently small plaquette admissibility bound; the principal formal result concerns SU(5) with 10⊕5-bar fermions, with specified restrictions to Standard Model groups and representations. Reflection positivity at finite spacing, full-current computational efficiency and an interacting continuum limit remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper describes prior nonperturbative nonabelian constructions as restricted to special representations or settings, while its reported construction covers the SU(5) generation representation and stated Standard Model restrictions. This is a source-reported mathematical comparison, not independent validation or practical simulation evidence.

The present record reports a candidate mathematical construction and author-reported formal verification, not practical simulation readiness or a completed interacting continuum theory.
